---
title: "Native Start migration runbook"
description: "How each web app except apps/web moves to TanStack Start + Void + Vite+ on Cloudflare Workers: ownership, the bridge, basePath readiness, acceptance gates, held publication, the canary ladder and rollback."
updatedAt: '2026-10-25'
---

Every web app except `apps/web` moves to its own TanStack Start + Void + Vite+
Worker on Cloudflare. `apps/web` stays on Next.js until separately scheduled.
The retired `apps/tanstack-web` tree is not part of this program and is not
revived. Current hosting (Vercel, or Next.js/OpenNext Workers) stays canonical
for an app until its explicit cutover PR merges.

## Ownership

- **One integration writer per app.** Only that lane edits the app's runtime,
  Worker entry, Vite/Void config and owning workflow. Other lanes hand changes
  to it.
- **`next/*` only through `@tuturuuu/start-bridge`.** App source keeps its App
  Router modules; the Vite preset aliases `next/*` to the bridge. Do not copy
  shims into the app. If the bridge lacks something, extend the package
  (additive within its frozen v0 contract) rather than forking it locally.
- **Registries are generated.** `start-bridge-routes check` runs in the app's CI
  and fails on any `route.*`/`page.*` that is not generated, owned by named
  native code, or ignored with a reason.
- Domain libraries stay framework-independent. Inject request identity,
  storage, navigation and localization at the adapter.

## basePath readiness

Each app must serve both its subdomain and `tuturuuu.com/<app>` from the same
source. `tuturuuu.com/<app>` is the app root; product marketing moves to
`/products/<app>`. Build with `TUTURUUU_BASE_PATH=/<app>` to produce the
path-mounted variant. The bridge supplies the asset base, server-function base,
router basepath, Location rewriting, base-aware links and auth return URLs.

Session cookies under a base are `tuturuuu_app_session__<app>` with
`Path=/<app>`, translated at the edge so auth code is unchanged. Sessions on a
legacy subdomain are host-only and are not carried to the shared origin: users
**re-login once at cutover**, unless a valid central (root) session silently
mints the new app session. There is no cross-host session handoff.

## Gates before cutover

An app is cutover-ready only with all of the following for the exact commit:

1. Exact-commit CI green: unit tests, type-check, lint, the registry check, a
   real `vp build`, and the app's owning native workflow.
2. Sealed emitted-Worker acceptance: the built artifact is hashed, its emitted
   config is validated, the emitted runtime suite passes, and a fresh restore
   of the same archive passes the same suite with unchanged bytes.
3. Staging acceptance on the owner-provisioned staging Worker: authentication
   and session refresh, MFA, workspace permissions, bilingual hydration, the
   app's primary flows, and both the subdomain and `/<app>` mounts.
4. A rollback record: the immutable prior deployment (artifact or deployment
   ID) and the captured routing (routes, custom domains and DNS records) that
   cutover replaces.

## Held publication and cutover

Production publication stays **held per app** in `productionPublicationPolicy`
(`tuturuuu.ci.ts`) until an explicit cutover PR admits that app. Deleting a
hold never admits publication. A cutover PR names the exact artifact, the
routing change and the rollback record, and merges only with the gates above.

Approvals:

- DNS, zone, canonical-route and staging-provider changes need release-authority
  approval.
- Database migrations need explicit user approval. The bridge itself needs none.

## Canary ladder

High-traffic apps (Tasks, Contacts and Finance) cut over only through the
canary ladder. Other apps may cut over directly once the gates pass.

| Step | Native share |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Staff only |
| 2 | 5% |
| 3 | 25% |
| 4 | 100% |

The share is `TUTURUUU_NATIVE_CANARY_PERCENT`; staff are admitted by forced
cohort. Assignment is sticky per browser (`tuturuuu_runtime_cohort`) and every
response carries `x-tuturuuu-runtime`.

**Advance** to the next step only after **at least 200 sessions and at least
4 hours** at the current step with every gate green. Compare the native cohort
against the legacy (control) cohort over the same window:

| Gate | Breach |
| --- | --- |
| Server errors | Native 5xx rate above control + 0.5 percentage points |
| Authentication | Any rise in auth loops or auth failures |
| Latency | Native p95 TTFB above 1.3 × control |
| Client errors | Native client error rate above 1.5 × control |

**Any breach sets the share to 0% automatically**, which returns all new and
sticky traffic to legacy. Investigate, fix forward, and restart the ladder from
staff only.

## Rollback

Rolling back an app restores the captured routing to the immutable prior
deployment. For a canaried app, setting the share to 0% is the first response.
Never delete the prior deployment or its routing record until the native
runtime has run at 100% through a full release cycle.
